title: Our Dining Table
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Salaryman Yutaka Hozumi, adopted as a child and told by his stepsiblings that eating with him was disgusting, has struggled to share meals with anyone. In a park he meets brothers Minoru and four-year-old Tane, who love his cooking and ask him to teach them. Cooking and eating together with the Ueda family, Yutaka and Minoru face their past loneliness and grow close. A single-volume boys' love story.
life_message: Sharing a table with people who welcome you can heal old wounds and make a family.

folkways.japan: The salaryman's isolation and the importance of eating together reflect Japanese discussions of koshoku (eating alone) and family meals.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls it 'charming'; summaries show healing through shared meals, not speeches (to verify).
delivery.note: The story carries its message through cooking and meals; the only cruelty shown is in Yutaka's past, and no argued opposing view appears.

winners_losers: Yutaka, Minoru and Tane form a family and win; the cruel stepsiblings of Yutaka's past are the only foils.
